description: Compare completed public verification success against independently observed replacement election preceding admission; fresh path is a permitted observational control, not a success liveness assertion.

harness.description: Actual handler reply held through F follower timeout and candidate election with N persisted vote, then actual L VerifyLeader admission and leaderLoop completion. Stop heartbeat before release, observe Future.Error for 300ms, then stop leaderLoop independently.
semantic_changes: Manual initial leader/configuration and worker wiring; no NewRaft startup or runLeader noop.
Injected transport executes receiver handlers and partitions election RPCs to L.
Only F heartbeat worker is run; N replication and normal append workers are not scheduled.
Heartbeat and leader lease timers on L are one hour; replacement F uses a validated 5ms heartbeat timeout and 200ms election timeout.

legality.derivation: VerifyLeader is specified to ensure the peer is still leader and prevent stale data after leadership loss. Under a static three-voter configuration, actual election of F in term 8 by its own vote and N vote before invocation means L in term 7 cannot validly confirm continued authority during this operation absent reacquisition. Therefore a completed verification on L must not report success solely on an earlier term-7 reply. This is a necessary negative condition in the observed replacement-election context, not a requirement for all replies to be fresh or for verification eventually to complete.
legality.applicability: Fixed voters L,F,N; pre-vote disabled for the replacement election; no L reelection, configuration change or newer reply during the verification interval; delayed genuine F response.
unresolved: Initial L leader state and committed configuration are fixtures; startup/election prefix not executed.
Ordinary replication and full runLeader setup are omitted; the controlled window represents their delay, without claiming all production schedules admit it.
Application reads and committed-log safety are excluded.
alternatives: Newer responses or incoming RPCs could step L down; those are absent in this selected schedule.
Pending verification is allowed. The oracle does not require eventual failure or success.
